logging/index.md: 'The `LogLevel` specifies the minimum level to log for selected categories.' Table: Information = 2, Warning = 3, levels listed 'from lowest to highest severity'. 'When a `LogLevel` is specified, logging is enabled for messages at the specified level and higher (more severe).' So Warning drops Information.

logging/index.md: 'The "Microsoft.AspNetCore" category applies to all categories that start with "Microsoft.AspNetCore".' How filtering rules are applied: 'select rules with longest matching category prefix.' Round 1 execution: appsettings Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore=Warning plus compose ...Database.Command=Information logged EventId 20101 at Information; re-confirmed by running efcore-sql.sh 2026-09-29.

EF Core 10 whatsnew l.643: 'When logging executed SQL, EF does not log parameter values by default, since these may contain sensitive or personally-identifiable information (PII); EnableSensitiveDataLogging can be used to enable logging parameter values in diagnostic or debugging scenarios'. extensions-logging.md: 'such data may be confidential'. Live output shows @customerId='?' etc.

EF Core 10 whatsnew l.645: 'EF sometimes inlines parameters into the SQL statement rather than sending them separately' (i.e. normally sent separately). Execution: same request with limit=1 returned only [{"id":6,...}] while the logged SQL still read 'LIMIT @p' with @p='?', so the value reached PostgreSQL outside the SQL text.

Opinion, supported: extensions-logging.md 'such data may be confidential, and could be revealed in production use'; EF 10 whatsnew limits EnableSensitiveDataLogging to 'diagnostic or debugging scenarios'. Matches depth_notes (not outside dev). The lesson gives the reason, so it is not an unconditioned recommendation.
